title: 实验 5-11 · 开漏输出 + 5 V 上拉：3.3 V 单片机输出 5 V 逻辑电平
summary: 耐 5 V 的 FT 引脚设成开漏输出，外接 4.7 kΩ 上拉到 5V：输出低 ≈ 0.04 V、灌 1 mA；“输出高”时引脚松开，上拉把它拉到 4.69 V——推挽输出只能给 3.3 V。起始电路用的是不耐 5 V 的 PA0。
description: **目标**：用 3.3 V 单片机的**开漏输出**加一个上拉电阻，给 5 V 逻辑芯片送出真正的 5 V 高电平，并看清楚为什么必须用耐 5 V 的引脚。
**电路**（Blue Pill 插在 USB 上）：
- R1（4.7 kΩ）：一端接开发板 **5V** 脚，另一端接结点 OUT5。
- OUT5 接一个 **FT（耐 5 V）引脚**（参考答案 PB12）。OUT5 就是要送给 5 V 逻辑芯片（例如 5 V 的 74HC 芯片、Arduino Uno 的输入）的信号。
- **起始状态**：上拉已经接好，但信号线接在 **PA0** 上，引脚设成开漏“高”。诊断报错“U1 PA0 上的电压太高：3.9 V”，保护二极管在往 3V3 灌 0.2 mA；判分也提示“PA0 不能当 GPIO_FT1 用”。把线换到一个 FT 引脚。
**引脚设置**：参考答案设为“输出高 + 开漏”；测试会依次设成开漏低、开漏高、推挽高。
**开漏是什么**：普通（推挽）输出里有两个开关：一个接 3.3 V，一个接 GND。开漏输出把接 3.3 V 的那个去掉了：
- **输出低**：下面的开关接通，引脚接地，从上拉电阻灌进电流。
- **输出高**：开关断开，引脚“松开”，电压由上拉电阻决定——拉到哪个电压就是哪个电压。
- **推挽输出高**：引脚自己输出 3.3 V。
**先预测**：5V 脚约 4.69 V，引脚开关导通时约 40 Ω。三种设置下 OUT5 各是多少伏？开漏低时引脚灌进多少电流？推挽高时，5 V 经上拉的电流往哪里流？5 V CMOS 输入的 VIH ≈ 0.7 × 5 V，哪种设置能被它认作高电平？
**测量**：开漏低的电压和灌电流、开漏高的电压（≈ 5 V，没有电流），推挽高的电压（只有 3.3 V）。电路检查通过后，把读数填进下面的「测量」（以你自己的面包板为准）；答完后会显示计算对比。
**上拉电阻怎么选**：
- 越小，上升沿越快（上升时间 ≈ 2.2 × R × C，100 pF 的线 + 输入电容时 4.7 kΩ ≈ 1 µs），但输出低时灌电流越大（5 V / R）。
- 越大，越省电，但越慢、越容易受干扰。1 kΩ–10 kΩ 是常用范围。
**实际项目经验**：
- **I²C 就是开漏总线**：SDA、SCL 都是开漏 + 上拉，所以不同芯片可以“线与”而不会打架。STM32 的 I²C 引脚 PB6–PB9、PB10/PB11 都是 FT，可以上拉到 5 V 直接和 5 V 器件通信（器件的 VIH 要满足）。
- **ESP32 不行**：它没有耐 5 V 的引脚，开漏上拉到 5 V 同样会通过保护二极管倒灌。要用 BSS138 MOSFET 双向电平转换模块（两侧各一个上拉：3.3 V 侧和 5 V 侧），或者把上拉接到 3.3 V，并确认 5 V 器件认 3.3 V 为高电平。
- 开漏也用来“线与”多个中断输出、驱动比 VDD 高电压的 LED（FT 引脚、5 V 侧）。
- 即使是 FT 引脚，开漏上拉到 5 V 时也**不要**同时打开内部上拉 / 下拉。
**模型说明**：输出级是 40 Ω 接 GND（开漏低）或高阻（开漏高）；保护二极管只接在非 FT 引脚上。仿真没有“5 V 逻辑输入”元件，用引脚电压对比 VIH 来判断。

en.title: Experiment 5-11 · Open-drain + 5 V pull-up: a 3.3 V MCU outputs a 5 V logic level
en.summary: A 5 V-tolerant FT pin as an open-drain output with an external 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 5V: LOW ≈ 0.04 V sinking 1 mA; at "HIGH" the pin lets go and the pull-up takes it to 4.69 V — push-pull only gives 3.3 V. The starting board uses PA0, which is not 5 V tolerant.
description: **Goal**: use a 3.3 V microcontroller's **open-drain output** plus one pull-up resistor to give a 5 V logic chip a real 5 V HIGH, and see why the pin must be 5 V tolerant.
**Circuit** (Blue Pill on USB):
- R1 (4.7 kΩ): one end to the board's **5V** pin, the other to node OUT5.
- OUT5 to an **FT (5 V-tolerant) pin** (the reference uses PB12). OUT5 is the signal for a 5 V logic chip (e.g. a 5 V 74HC chip or an Arduino Uno input).

- **Starting board**: the pull-up is in place but the signal goes to **PA0**, set to open-drain "high". The diagnostics say "U1 PA0 voltage is too high: 3.9 V" with the clamp diode pushing 0.2 mA into 3V3; the checker also says "PA0 can't be used as GPIO_FT1". Move the wire to an FT pin.
**Pin table settings**: the reference sets output HIGH + open-drain; the tests use open-drain LOW, open-drain HIGH and push-pull HIGH in turn.
**What open-drain means**: a normal (push-pull) output has two switches, one to 3.3 V and one to GND. An open-drain output drops the one to 3.3 V:
- **Output LOW**: the lower switch closes, the pin is grounded and sinks current from the pull-up.
- **Output HIGH**: the switch opens and the pin "lets go"; the pull-up decides the voltage — whatever it is tied to.
- **Push-pull HIGH**: the pin drives 3.3 V itself.

**Predict first**: the 5V pin is about 4.69 V and the pin's switch is about 40 Ω when on. What is OUT5 in each of the three settings? How much current does the pin sink at open-drain LOW? At push-pull HIGH, where does the current from 5 V through the pull-up go? A 5 V CMOS input has VIH ≈ 0.7 × 5 V: which setting does it accept as HIGH?

**Measure**: the open-drain LOW voltage and sink current, the open-drain HIGH voltage (≈ 5 V, no current) and the push-pull HIGH voltage (only 3.3 V). Once the circuit check passes, type your readings into the Measurements below (whatever your own board shows); the worked comparison appears after you answer.
**Choosing the pull-up**:
- Smaller is faster (rise time ≈ 2.2 × R × C; with 100 pF of wiring and input capacitance 4.7 kΩ gives ≈ 1 µs) but sinks more current at LOW (5 V / R).
- Larger saves power but is slower and picks up more noise. 1 kΩ–10 kΩ is the usual range.
**Rule of thumb for real projects**:

- **I²C is an open-drain bus**: SDA and SCL are open-drain + pull-up, so several chips can share a line ("wired-AND") without fighting. The STM32's I²C pins PB6–PB9 and PB10/PB11 are FT, so the bus can be pulled up to 5 V to talk to 5 V parts directly (as long as their VIH is met).

- **The ESP32 can't do this**: it has no 5 V-tolerant pins, so an open-drain pin pulled up to 5 V back-feeds through its clamp diode too. Use a BSS138 MOSFET bidirectional level-shifter module (one pull-up on each side, 3.3 V and 5 V), or pull up to 3.3 V and check the 5 V part accepts 3.3 V as HIGH.
- Open-drain is also used to wire-AND several interrupt outputs and to sink LEDs from a supply above VDD (FT pin, 5 V side).
- Even on an FT pin, do **not** enable the internal pull-up / pull-down when it is pulled up to 5 V.

**Model note**: the output stage is 40 Ω to GND (open-drain LOW) or high impedance (open-drain HIGH); clamp diodes exist only on non-FT pins. There is no "5 V logic input" part, so the pin voltage is compared with VIH by hand.
compare: - Open-drain LOW: V = **0.04 V**, sinking **0.99 mA** (= 4.69 V / 4.7 kΩ).
- Open-drain HIGH: V = **4.69 V** (the 5V pin), zero pin current.
- Push-pull HIGH: only **3.31 V**, and **0.29 mA** flows back from 5 V through the pull-up into the pin. With VIH ≈ **3.5 V**, a 5 V CMOS input may not count 3.3 V as HIGH.

**Why it must be an FT pin**: at open-drain "high" the pin sees 5 V. A normal pin has a clamp diode to 3V3 that holds OUT5 at about 3.9 V (3.3 V + one diode drop), with current flowing from 5 V through the pull-up and the diode into 3V3 — it can't output 5 V and it back-feeds the supply. An FT pin has no such diode and withstands 5 V.

measurements.explain: The N-channel switch is about 40 Ω: 40 Ω × 0.99 mA ≈ 40 mV.

measurements.ask: Open-drain LOW: the current in the pull-up R1 (the current the pin sinks)
measurements.explain: 4.69 V / 4.7 kΩ ≈ 0.99 mA. A smaller pull-up gives faster edges but more sink current in LOW.

measurements.ask: Open-drain HIGH (pin released): OUT5 to GND
measurements.explain: The pin lets go, R1 carries no current, and OUT5 equals the 5V pin's 4.69 V — an FT pin has no clamp diode to 3V3, so nothing holds it down.

measurements.ask: Push-pull HIGH instead: OUT5 to GND
measurements.explain: The high-side switch holds OUT5 at about 3.3 V, below a 5 V CMOS input's VIH ≈ 3.5 V: it may not count as HIGH.

measurements.ask: Same state: the current in R1 (from the 5V pin toward the pin)
measurements.explain: (4.69 − 3.31) / 4.7 kΩ ≈ 0.29 mA flows back from 5 V into the pin and on into 3V3: push-pull is fighting the 5 V pull-up.

hints: Start: PA0 is not 5 V tolerant. Move the signal wire to a lower-row FT pin such as PB12.
Only one resistor: 4.7 kΩ from the 5V pin to the signal node.
In the pin table choose output HIGH and tick "open-drain".
tests: Open-drain LOW: close to 0 V, sinking the pull-up current
Open-drain HIGH: the pin lets go, the pull-up takes it to the 5V pin voltage, no current (FT pin, no clamp diode)
Push-pull HIGH instead: only 3.3 V, and current flows back into the pin

tests.name: 开漏输出低：接近 0 V，从上拉灌入电流
开漏输出高：引脚松开，上拉拉到 5V 脚的电压，没有电流（FT 引脚，没有保护二极管）
换成推挽输出高：只有 3.3 V，电流倒流进引脚

compare: - 推挽高：只有 **3.31 V**，还会有 **0.29 mA** 从 5 V 经上拉倒流进引脚。5 V CMOS 输入的 VIH ≈ **3.5 V**，3.3 V 不一定能被认作高电平。
**为什么必须是 FT 引脚**：开漏“高”时引脚上是 5 V。普通引脚内部有接 3V3 的保护二极管，会把 OUT5 钳在约 3.9 V（3.3 V + 二极管压降），电流从 5 V 经上拉、二极管灌进 3V3——既输出不了 5 V，又在倒灌电源。FT 引脚没有这个二极管，可以承受 5 V。

measurements.ask: 开漏输出低：OUT5 对 GND 的电压
开漏输出低：上拉 R1 的电流（也就是引脚灌进的电流）
measurements.explain: 4.69 V / 4.7 kΩ ≈ 0.99 mA。上拉越小上升沿越快，但输出低时灌电流越大。

measurements.ask: 开漏输出高（引脚松开）：OUT5 对 GND
measurements.explain: 引脚不再拉，R1 里没有电流，OUT5 等于 5V 脚的 4.69 V——FT 引脚没有接 3V3 的保护二极管，所以不会被钳住。

measurements.ask: 改成推挽输出高：OUT5 对 GND
measurements.explain: 上管把 OUT5 拉在约 3.3 V，低于 5 V CMOS 的 VIH ≈ 3.5 V：不一定能被认作高电平。

measurements.ask: 同一状态：R1 的电流（从 5V 脚流向引脚）
measurements.explain: (4.69 − 3.31) / 4.7 kΩ ≈ 0.29 mA 从 5 V 倒流进引脚、再灌进 3V3：推挽和 5 V 上拉在打架。

hints: 起始电路：PA0 不耐 5 V。把信号线换到下排的 FT 引脚，例如 PB12。
只要一个电阻：4.7 kΩ 从 5V 脚接到信号结点。
在引脚表里选“输出高电平”，并勾选“开漏”。
